gen-dafont-over-there-gf-new-tegomin: New Tegomin gives its c a wide, ring-like opening, dignified and traditional in tone. Over There, cut at a single depth like an engraver's tool, adds a vintage-military bark overhead.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-podkova: Vintage-military Over There draws tubular strokes that look like bent copper pipe, with plenty of space between letters. Podkova settles in underneath with a broad, welcoming c and a bookish, traditional manner.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-rokkitt: Over There looks drawn by a fixed-width nib, each stroke carrying the weight of drawn wire. But Rokkitt, bookish and traditional, with its paperclip-open c, gives the whole thing a stern, old-world steadiness.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-sanchez: Over There draws thin-looking letters with no thinner parts anywhere, vintage-military and commanding in spirit, with generous white space between them. Sanchez, bookish and dignified, has a c spread like calipers.
gen-dafont-over-there-gf-solway: Commanding Over There letters look drawn with a fixed-width nib, spaced generously apart. Solway, authoritative and bookish, keeps its line weight flat like a sign-painter's stencil, with a generous entry into the e.
gen-dafont-ozone-fs-quicksand: The body text reads approachable, with bulb-round lowercase bowls and bars of identical thickness along the line. Quicksand then backs up Ozone, whose geometric headings carry wide-set curve ends.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-fanwood-text: Ozone traces each letter in a line of constant weight, technical and geometric, with wide-set curve ends. Fanwood Text handles the bookish side, with large-eyed lowercase and gently swelling curves.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-naskh-arabic: Ozone keeps its n arches no lighter than the stems beside them, so the geometric, technical letters feel plainly constructed. Noto Naskh Arabic is the softer voice, with a mild shimmer of weight.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-nastaliq-urdu: Technical and geometric, Ozone draws a plain, unshaded line that never swells, with wide-set curve ends in every round form. Noto Nastaliq Urdu brings mild stress, editorial and dignified, that the heading lacks.
gen-dafont-ozone-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Noto Rashi Hebrew reads classic and bookish, a serif with modest contrast like lightly engraved brass lettering. And Ozone, geometric and technical, does its best work big and short.
